title: Rigveda 5.16: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.16: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.16 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 332v-333r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>bṛ̱had vayo̱ hi bhā̱nave 'rcā̍ de̱vāyā̱gnaye̍ | yam mi̱traṁ na praśa̍stibhi̱r martā̍so dadhi̱re pu̱raḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>GREAT power is in the beam of light, sing praise to, Agni, to the God Whom men have set in foremost place like Mitra with their eulogies.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 332v (numbered 5v by the scribe) (OPenn image 333, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.15.3 ‹-nava-jātaḥ tuturyāt siṃham na›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 333r (numbered 6r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.16.2 ‹-ṛṇvati›. Verse 5.16.1 ends on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 5.16.2-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 333r
translation.original_text:
2sa hi dyubhi̱r janā̍nā̱ṁ hotā̱ dakṣa̍sya bā̱hvoḥ | vi ha̱vyam a̱gnir ā̍nu̱ṣag bhago̱ na vāra̍m ṛṇvati ||
3a̱sya stome̍ ma̱ghona̍ḥ sa̱khye vṛ̱ddhaśo̍ciṣaḥ | viśvā̱ yasmi̍n tuvi̱ṣvaṇi̱ sam a̱rye śuṣma̍m āda̱dhuḥ ||
4adhā̱ hy a̍gna eṣāṁ su̱vīrya̍sya ma̱ṁhanā̍ | tam id ya̱hvaṁ na roda̍sī̱ pari̱ śravo̍ babhūvatuḥ ||
5nū na̱ ehi̱ vārya̱m agne̍ gṛṇā̱na ā bha̍ra | ye va̱yaṁ ye ca̍ sū̱raya̍ḥ sva̱sti dhāma̍he̱ saco̱taidhi̍ pṛ̱tsu no̍ vṛ̱dhe ||
translation.text:
2He by the splendour of his arms is Priest of every able man. Agni conveys oblation straight, and deals, as Bhaga deals, his boons.
3All rests upon the laud and love of him the rich, high-flaming God, On whom, loud-roaring, men have laid great strength as on a faithful friend.
4So, Agni, be the Friend of these with liberal gift of hero strength. Yea, Heaven and Earth have not surpassed this Youthful One in glorious fame.
5O Agni, quickly come to us, and, glorified, bring precious wealth. So we and these our princes will assemble for the good of all. Be near in fight to prosper us.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 333r (numbered 6r by the scribe) (OPenn image 333, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.16.2 ‹-ṛṇvati›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 333v (numbered 6v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.17.3 ‹yaḥ ayukta tujā girā›. Verses 5.16.2-5 end on this page; 5.16.2 begins on fol. 332v (numbered 5v by the scribe).

3asya | stome | maghonaḥ | sakhye | vṛddha-śociṣaḥ | viśvā | yasmin | tuvi-svaṇi | sam | arye | śuṣmam | ādadhuḥ
